nodes.label: Technical Guidelines for SSF Data Harmonization in the WIO Region
SSF Data Harmonization
nodes.rationale: Harmonization does not require forcing all organizations into a single identical form; it identifies a core set of overlapping variables and common definitions enabling cross-dataset comparison while preserving each programme's flexibility. It strengthens SSF visibility in governance, positions organizations for multi-country funding, reduces data-cleaning burden, and scales local impact to regional narratives on food security, livelihoods, and climate resilience.

nodes.label: Regional Scoping Assessment (26 institutions, 10 WIO countries)
nodes.rationale: Scoping assessment of 26 institutions across ten WIO countries found 88% capture catch/effort and 84% vessel/gear data, but only 48% collect socio-economic data; 88% use consistent internal standards yet only 28% are compatible with external institutions; financial sustainability (68%) was the top challenge. Established that the region has a solid data-collection foundation but lacks coordination mechanisms.

nodes.label: Integrated Data Harmonization Framework (IDHF)
nodes.rationale: Three-phase conceptual framework (Tungpantong et al., 2021): (1) Diagnostic Assessment, (2) Design and Standardization, (3) Implementation and Sustainability. The guidelines operationalize all three phases into actionable technical specifications.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Survey of Current Data Collection Practices (Phase I)
nodes.rationale: A participatory, institution-level survey is required to map what entities currently measure, how they define variables, and what tools they use, before a minimum variable set is adopted. This grounds harmonization in operational realities rather than imposing it top-down, so the minimum common denominator reflects the genuine intersection of existing efforts. Recommended via a structured digital form (e.g. Airtable).

nodes.label: Minimum Common Denominator (Minimum Variable Set)
nodes.rationale: A core set of consistently defined variables every institution must provide, representing the intersection of what all institutions can feasibly contribute. It enables cross-dataset comparison and regional aggregation without constraining institutions from collecting additional variables beyond the core set. Final specification to be determined collaboratively via the diagnostic survey and validated by the WGDS.

nodes.label: Fishery-level Contextual Information for Scaling Up
nodes.rationale: Census-type data on the number of active fishers and boats per landing site provide the denominators needed to raise sample-based catch/effort data to population-level totals; standardized landing-site metadata (unique location codes, coordinates aligned with FAO GAUL) enable spatial aggregation and accurate mapping across the WIO.

nodes.label: Standardized Sampling Methodologies
nodes.rationale: Standardizing variables alone is insufficient if underlying sampling designs are incompatible; comparable sampling requires aligned sampling-frame definition, stratification, temporal/spatial coverage documentation, raising procedures, and QA/QC so data from different institutions can be meaningfully compared and aggregated.

nodes.label: Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC) Procedures
Functional Requirements for Electronic Data Collection Tools
nodes.rationale: Paper-based collection is error-prone, slow, locally confined, and offers no real-time validation; digital collection enables immediate sync, built-in validation at point of entry, and automatic export to analysis pipelines. Requirements are defined tool-agnostically (not mandating one platform) since 88% of institutions already use digital platforms, indicating readiness for a coordinated transition.

nodes.label: Centralized Data Pipelines
nodes.rationale: Tool-agnostic pipelines accept data from multiple collection platforms and apply standardized transformation, validation, and formatting before ingesting records into a central/regional repository, accommodating the diversity of tools in use while ensuring all data converge to a common standard at aggregation.

nodes.label: Ontologies and Classification Systems
nodes.rationale: Ontologies provide the semantic infrastructure ensuring each variable name carries a single clear definition across institutions; by mapping data elements to internationally recognized identifiers and hierarchies they resolve terminological ambiguities and enable machine-readable interoperability between datasets using different local labels for the same concept.

nodes.label: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
FAO International Standard Statistical Classification of Fishing Gear (ISSCFG)
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical gear coding (first-tier categories e.g. 'Gillnets and Entangling Nets' code 07; second-tier e.g. 'Set gillnets (anchored)' GNS 07.1). Adoption resolves ambiguity where the same equipment is recorded under different local names (e.g. 'Monofilament Nets' vs 'Gillnets') across organizations. Documented in FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Technical Paper No. 672.

nodes.label: FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Technical Paper No. 672
FAO ASFIS List and 3-alpha Codes
nodes.rationale: FAO Aquatic Sciences and Fisheries Information System assigns each species a unique three-letter code (e.g. PIL for Sardina pilchardus), providing unambiguous identifiers that bridge linguistic and taxonomic discrepancies. Organizations should adopt a shared reference pairing local and scientific names to FAO 3-alpha codes.

nodes.label: FAO Global Administrative Unit Layers (GAUL)
nodes.rationale: Landing sites and administrative units referenced to FAO GAUL (FAO, 2024) ensure consistent spatial coding across countries and enable spatial aggregation at sub-national, national, and regional scales.

nodes.label: ISO 8601 Date/Time Standard
nodes.rationale: All date fields recorded in YYYY-MM-DD format to ensure unambiguous temporal referencing and full interoperability across datasets and software systems.

nodes.label: Aquatic Food Ontology (AQFO)
nodes.rationale: A formally structured vocabulary providing semantic definitions and hierarchical relationships for fisheries concepts (gear, fishing net, line, trap, fuel). Each concept has a unique URI (e.g. http://w3id.org/aqfo/aqfo_00002220 for 'gear'). Linking each data-dictionary variable to its AQFO URI gives every variable a machine-readable, unambiguous definition; adoption recommended as a medium-term goal.

nodes.label: Regional Data Dictionary
nodes.rationale: A shared reference framework co-created with SWIOFC and the WGDS defining core variables, metadata structures, classification systems, and standardized terminologies so all participating countries/institutions work from an aligned vocabulary. Maintained as a living document, updated periodically to reflect evolving needs and new international standards.

nodes.label: Data-Sharing Agreements
nodes.rationale: Legally binding agreements between primary data custodians defining access levels, privacy rules, data ownership, custodianship roles, and shared repository arrangements. 81.8% of scoping respondents support open access with appropriate safeguards, indicating readiness for formalized data-sharing.

nodes.label: Regional Data Governance Board
nodes.rationale: Recommended potentially under SWIOFC auspices to finalize rules on data ownership, access rights, licensing, and long-term hosting, clarifying responsibilities of collectors, validators, custodians, and users (custodianship is currently centralized in fisheries departments in 80% of cases).

nodes.label: South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission (SWIOFC)
Working Group on Data and Statistics (WGDS)
Phased Implementation Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Six-phase roadmap from 2026 to 2030+: (1) Diagnostic survey Q4 2026–Q1 2027; (2) Standardization Q2–Q3 2027; (3) Pilot testing in Kenya/Mozambique/Zanzibar Q3 2027–Q2 2028; (4) Evaluation Q3 2028; (5) Regional rollout to all SWIOFC member states Q4 2028–Q4 2029; (6) Sustained operation 2030 onwards.
